what_it_does: Analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) convert real-world signals like microphone audio into digital numbers. Pipelined ADCs process samples in stages, but suffer from gain errors (each stage amplifies the signal differently than intended) and nonlinearity (the relationship between input and output is curved, not flat). This paper proposes a real-time calibration technique using piecewise-linear (PWL) approximation—dividing the input range into segments and fitting each segment with its own correction formula. The technique runs in the background without interrupting normal operation, avoiding the power and area cost of polynomial-based methods, and uses adaptive thresholds to prioritize which signal ranges need the most correction.
